newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares edge up, bolstered by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares edge up, bolstered by Wall Street.

text.p: Singapore shares edged upwards in early trading on Wednesday with sentiment bolstered by an overnight record high on Wall Street, dealers said.
"The market is basically being led by Wall Street, where the momentum has been building over Christmas and the New Year," one dealer said.
Early gains in the first 90 minutes of trading saw Singapore's key Straits Times Industrials Index creep up 1.59 points to 2,248.18 with blue chips and property stocks favoured.
Some second line activity was also forecast by dealers for later in the day as positive sentiment spread.
"It looks like being a good year for the market -- it's certainly a good start," said the dealer, who added the warning that "last year we started out very strong but then fizzled out."
Early momentum saw 51.2 million shares traded in the opening exchanges, producing 158 gainers against 58 losers.
Leading gainers were Creative Technology, up Singapore $0.60 at S$15.50 and the foreign share tranches of banks OCBC and DBS, both up S$0.40 at S$18.20 and S$19.40 respectively.
